scope_declines.name: Lemma 8.20: sections of O_W on the preimage of an affine open via base change
scope_declines.reason: The tensor-section computation is needed only for the scheme-level affine-local proof of finiteness; the classical page defines finiteness directly by affine inverse images, so this lemma is not a prerequisite of any scaffolded item.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 31.34.4 (strict transforms commute with affine morphisms after blowup)
scope_declines.reason: Affine-morphism compatibility of strict transforms is not used by any claim on this pair; strict transforms here are handled by the scheme-theoretic closure definition and the chart saturation.

scope_declines.name: §9.7.4: warning on when integral closure can fail to be finite
scope_declines.reason: The warning marks the boundary of the finiteness theorem for non-excellent bases; this pair works over a field, where the published CA-19 finiteness theorem already applies, so the warning supports no item.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 33.45.6 (tag 0BES): additivity over irreducible components with multiplicities
scope_declines.reason: No local item pairs a line bundle with a possibly nonreduced curve by multiplicities; the restriction theorem treats effective Cartier divisors directly.

scope_declines.name: §19.4.10–19.4.11 remarks on non-isomorphic small resolutions and factorization of birational maps
scope_declines.reason: Minimal-model-style discussion of factorizations and small resolutions lies beyond the pair scope; no assigned claim depends on it and it is not scaffolded.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 33.44.4 (tag 0AYU): degree is invariant under birational morphisms of proper curves
scope_declines.reason: The devissage proof of degree additivity used here avoids the birational comparison, and no commissioned item needs invariance under birational morphisms.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 33.44.6 (tag 0AYW): degree decomposes over irreducible components with multiplicities
scope_declines.reason: The scaffold proves additivity directly by devissage on the whole curve, so the component-multiplicity reduction is not needed by any local item.

scope_declines.name: Proposition 8.25: base change of a finite map is finite
scope_declines.reason: Base-change stability of finiteness is a scheme-level statement not consumed by this pair; the finite morphisms used here are compared on a fixed target by their defining affine charts.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 31.34.7 (strict transforms of universally exact sequences stay exact)
scope_declines.reason: Universally exact sequences of modules under strict transform are a technical flatness-descent tool; no proof on this pair passes through it, so it is not retained.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 31.34.6 (description of strict transforms under a composite of two blowups)
scope_declines.reason: The resolution argument applies the strict-transform definition at each step separately and never needs the two-step strict-transform description recorded in this lemma.

scope_declines.name: 8.58–8.60: bijective regular maps and continuity of inverses
scope_declines.reason: The bijectivity-versus-isomorphism discussion for arbitrary regular maps is not needed: the pair's finite birational statement is supplied by 8.57 and its finite refinement, and the cusp counterexample records the failure without target normality.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 33.45.1 (tag 0BEM): chi(X, F (x) L_1^{n_1} (x) ... ) is a numerical polynomial of total degree <= dim Supp F
scope_declines.reason: The scaffold defines the pairing by the alternating sum and proves bilinearity through the effective-divisor shift identity; the numerical-polynomial route is a different, equally valid proof and is not needed locally.

scope_declines.name: 8.30–8.33: first quasi-finite and integrality examples
scope_declines.reason: The projection of xy=1, power maps, and the Frobenius variants illustrate quasi-finiteness but are not used by any scaffolded item; the one example this page needs from the block is 8.34, harvested separately.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 33.45.9 (tag 0BEV) and Definition 33.45.10 (tag 0BEW): positivity and degree with respect to an ample bundle
scope_declines.reason: Positivity and the degree of a subscheme with respect to an ample polarization are ampleness-page material and no commissioned item or example invokes them.

scope_declines.name: Exercise 20.2.C (the intersection form of P^1 x P^1)
scope_declines.reason: The design freezes the B page to the projective plane and its point blowup; the P^1 x P^1 computation is a natural later example but no commissioned item consumes it.

scope_declines.name: §4.6 Chevalley's Finiteness Theorem
scope_declines.reason: Chevalley's finiteness theorem states the proper-quasi-finite finiteness in the scheme register owned by the later finite-proper-and-projective-morphisms page; this page proves the classical case through its local bridge.

scope_declines.name: Lemmas 31.36.1–31.36.3 (blowing up Fitting ideals: the strict transform of a finite type module becomes locally free)
scope_declines.reason: Fitting-ideal blowups flatten modules; the pair has no flattening claim, and the only flatness input it uses is the hypothesis of the flat-base-change theorem.

scope_declines.name: Theorems 37.16.1–37.16.2 and Lemmas 37.16.3–37.16.8 (critère de platitude par fibres: flatness of a morphism tested on fibres)
scope_declines.reason: Fibre-wise flatness criteria are not used: the pair assumes flatness where needed and never needs to test or produce it, so these results are not built here.

scope_declines.name: §9.7.1: rings of integers in number fields as the basic example of normalization
scope_declines.reason: The number-field remark illustrates normalization outside algebraic geometry proper; the pair's normalization examples are the cusp and the node, and no scaffolded item consumes rings of integers.

scope_declines.name: Lemmas 33.44.10-33.44.15 (divisibility of degrees, positivity, and ampleness and section criteria on curves)
scope_declines.reason: Section criteria, positivity and the ampleness characterisation of degrees on curves belong to the curve pages already published in this run and are not consumed by this pair.

scope_declines.name: §h historical outline: surfaces over C by Walker and Zariski, characteristic zero threefolds by Zariski, nonzero characteristic by Abhyankar, all varieties in characteristic zero by Hironaka, de Jong's alteration theorem
scope_declines.reason: A historical survey of resolution in dimensions beyond curves; the pair states resolution only for plane curves and explicitly disclaims higher-dimensional or arbitrary-field smooth resolution.

scope_declines.name: Corollary 8.16: extending a regular map defined outside a codimension-two closed set
scope_declines.reason: The extension theorem for maps to affine varieties is not consumed by any item of this pair; the codimension-two consequence the page actually needs is the rational-function case 8.15, which is built separately.

scope_declines.name: Proposition 8.26: finite maps are proper
scope_declines.reason: Properness and its interaction with finiteness are owned by the later finite-proper-and-projective-morphisms page (order 366.069); this earlier page uses closedness and finite fibres directly instead.

scope_declines.name: Exercise 20.1.B (invariance of the product under field extension)
scope_declines.reason: The scaffold states all four A items directly over an arbitrary field and never compares intersections across a field extension, so no commissioned item consumes this invariance.

scope_declines.name: Summary 8.13: the nonsingular/factorial/normal dictionary
scope_declines.reason: This is a summary sentence rather than a proof obligation: each of its component implications (regular is normal, normal has codimension-two singular locus, curves) is harvested separately above and below, so a separate item would duplicate them.

scope_declines.name: §29.6.3: pointers to other versions of the theorem and EGA references
scope_declines.reason: This is a bibliographic pointer paragraph rather than a mathematical result; the EGA corollary it points to is recorded as a separate source row with its exact numeration.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 31.34.5 (blowing up in the product of the ideals of Z and an effective Cartier divisor D gives the blowup in Z)
scope_declines.reason: A sibling form of the invariance of blowups under invertible rescalings; the pair covers that invariance once through Lemma 31.33.12 and does not need this second presentation.

scope_declines.name: Exercise 18.6.A (a very ample section can be chosen nonvanishing at the associated points)
scope_declines.reason: The scaffold closes multilinearity through eventual global generation and differences of effective divisors, so the avoidance statement is not needed by any local item.

scope_declines.name: Definition 8.10 and Proposition 8.11: factorial points and locally principal prime divisors
scope_declines.reason: Factoriality of local rings and the prime-divisor characterisation belong to the commutative-algebra divisor track; the AV-7 contract consumes only normality, so no item is minted here and no later proof of this page uses factoriality.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 33.45.2 (tag 0BEN): the leading coefficient depends on lengths at generic points
scope_declines.reason: The leading-coefficient computation serves the positivity and degree theory of subschemes, neither of which is part of the commissioned inventory.

scope_declines.name: Corollary 8.27: the source of a finite map to a complete variety is complete
scope_declines.reason: Completeness (properness) of the source is not part of the AV-7 contract and is supplied later; the pair proves closedness and finite fibres only, which is what its consumers use.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 31.33.3 (tag 0805): flat base change of blowups
scope_declines.reason: Base change of blowups is proved on the selected blowup page as thm-blowup-base-change-flat and is not part of the intersection-product argument.

scope_declines.name: Aside 8.44 and 8.52: a finite map onto a normal variety is open
scope_declines.reason: Openness of finite maps onto normal targets is a geometric refinement not consumed by this pair; the universal property and the birational-isomorphism lemma are proved without it.

scope_declines.name: Definition 31.33.1 (tag 01OF): the blowup b: X' -> X of a closed subscheme, with twists O_{X'}(n)
scope_declines.reason: The construction is built by item def-blowup-scheme-along-ideal on the selected batch-2 page blowups-exceptional-divisors-and-strict-transforms, which this page requires; the local item consumes it as a supplier.

scope_declines.name: §19.3.4 aside on the two approaches to existence
scope_declines.reason: An expository comparison of the Proj and closure constructions; it states no result the pair needs, so it is deliberately not made into an item.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 33.45.9 (tag 0BEV): positivity for ample line bundles
scope_declines.reason: No example on the B page uses positivity; the computations are explicit via the cohomology of twists on projective space.

scope_declines.name: §19.4.5–19.4.6 remarks on ADE surface singularities and general resolution of singularities
scope_declines.reason: These are survey remarks pointing beyond curves on surfaces; the pair explicitly disclaims higher-dimensional resolution and builds no item from them.

scope_declines.name: §4.7 Double Planes
scope_declines.reason: Double-plane constructions are a surface-specific application that feeds no item or consumer of this pair, as recorded in the track's deliberately-not-decomposed table.

scope_declines.name: §20.2.9 (the self-intersection of a fibre of a fibration is zero)
scope_declines.reason: Fibrations of surfaces and the relative Picard formalism are outside this pair, and no consumer on the two pages uses a fibre class.

scope_declines.name: Proposition 33.45.13 (tag 0BJ8): asymptotic Riemann-Roch
scope_declines.reason: Asymptotic Riemann-Roch belongs to the Hilbert-polynomial and Chow-group developments and is not used by the four design items.

scope_declines.name: 8.55: closed quasi-finite maps of curves that are not finite
scope_declines.reason: The example of a closed but not universally closed quasi-finite map is not consumed by any item; the properness criterion is proved from the factorization instead.

scope_declines.name: Theorem 8.43: fibre cardinality bounds for finite surjective maps onto a normal base
scope_declines.reason: The separable-degree bound is a normal-base refinement of finiteness; this pair uses only closedness and finite fibres, and no scaffolded item or consumer states the cardinality bound.

scope_declines.name: 8.35–8.39: further quasi-finite examples and the cusp/nodal illustrations
scope_declines.reason: These examples (Frobenius, degree-two maps between curves and their ideal-theoretic variants) are illustrative computations; the pair's examples are the cusp, the node and the punctured-plane map, and no proof depends on the others.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 33.44.2 (tag 0B59): degree is unchanged by field extension
scope_declines.reason: No local item states a change-of-field comparison for degrees; the four A items are stated over an arbitrary fixed field.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 31.34.3 (flatness over the center makes the strict transform equal to the base change)
scope_declines.reason: This is a flat-base-change statement for strict transforms; the pair uses only the flat base change of the blowup itself (Lemma 31.33.3) and the nonflat failure example, not this variant.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 31.33.10 (bijection between generic points of the blowup and generic points of X outside Z)
scope_declines.reason: The pair never needs generic-point bookkeeping of blowups: birationality is proved through the off-center isomorphism and integrality through the Rees charts, so this result is deliberately not built here.

scope_declines.name: 8.50: replacing the finite model by the closure of the image
scope_declines.reason: The closure refinement of the factorization is cosmetic for the classical use here; the bridge items produce the open immersion into a finite model directly and no consumer needs dominance of the model.

scope_declines.name: Example 8.41 and Lemma 8.42: separating finitely many points by a regular function
scope_declines.reason: Separating points by regular functions belongs to the later quasi-affineness treatment and is not used by any item of this pair; finiteness is characterised here through coordinate modules instead.

scope_declines.name: Exercise 20.1.K (positivity of the product with ample line bundles)
scope_declines.reason: Positivity needs the Nakai-Moishezon criterion or an embedding-degree argument; it belongs to the ampleness page and is not part of this pair's design inventory.

scope_declines.name: Definition 31.35.1 and Lemmas 31.35.2–31.35.6 (U-admissible blowups: definition, projectivity, base change, composition)
scope_declines.reason: Admissible blowups are a device for blowup presentations in flatness and descent arguments; this pair uses ordinary blowups of ideals, their universal property and their charts, not the admissible-blowup formalism.

scope_declines.name: Summary 8.22: equivalent conditions for finiteness
scope_declines.reason: Another summary list; the equivalent conditions it collects are EGA-style properness and affineness statements owned by the later finite-proper-and-projective-morphisms page, not by this classical pair.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 31.33.14 (the composite of two blowups is again a blowup along a finite type ideal)
scope_declines.reason: Our resolution theorem composes point blowups inductively and only needs each individual step; describing the composite as one blowup in a larger ideal is not required and is left unbuilt.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 20 (Chow's lemma: a complete irreducible variety is birational to a projective variety)
scope_declines.reason: Chow's lemma is a completeness/projectivity device; the pair works with explicit blowups of surfaces and curves and never needs a birational projective model.

scope_declines.name: Proposition 20.1.6 (dependence only on numerical equivalence)
scope_declines.reason: Numerical equivalence is not developed on these two pages and none of the commissioned items or examples needs invariance beyond linear equivalence, which the definition records.

scope_declines.name: Exercise 20.1.C(b) (recovery of Bezout for hypersurfaces)
scope_declines.reason: The design explicitly forbids repeating the AV-8 plane-curve Bezout development; the projective-space computations live on the examples companion of this pair instead.

scope_declines.name: §4.5 Dimension
scope_declines.reason: Dimension theory for varieties is owned by the published AV-5 pair dimension-constructible-images-and-dimensions-of-fibres (order 366.057), which this page already requires; re-minting it here would duplicate content.

scope_declines.name: Exercise 20.1.I (asymptotic Riemann-Roch; the leading coefficient is an intersection number)
scope_declines.reason: The coefficient interpretation requires the numerical-polynomial lemma and Chern-class asymptotics that belong to the later Chow-groups pair, not to the four commissioned items.

scope_declines.name: Exercise 20.2.A(b) (length of the scheme-theoretic intersection when C avoids the associated points of D)
scope_declines.reason: The length description needs the Cohen-Macaulay behaviour of divisors on a regular surface and duplicates the plane-curve intersection page, which the design tells this pair not to repeat.

scope_declines.name: Lemmas 37.18.1–37.18.5 and Remark 37.18.6 (flat modules and relative assassins)
scope_declines.reason: Relative assassins of flat modules belong to a different development of flatness theory; nothing on this pair states or proves a result in which they appear.

scope_declines.name: Exercise 20.2.C (P^1 x P^1)
scope_declines.reason: The examples companion is fixed to P^2 and its point blowup by the design, so the P^1 x P^1 form is not built here.

scope_declines.name: Theorem 8.40: finite surjective maps and the discriminant bound on fibres
scope_declines.reason: The separable-degree fibre bound is a refinement not consumed by the AV-7 items; the page records only closedness and finite fibres, and no consumer needs the enumerated fibre bound.

scope_declines.name: Exercise 20.2.B (adjunction and Riemann-Roch for surfaces)
scope_declines.reason: This is precisely the immediately following selected pair AG-SURF-2 at plan order 897, whose design items are exactly the surface Riemann-Roch theorem and the Hodge index theorem; building it here would duplicate that page.

scope_declines.name: §9.7.I: exercise on normalization in a function-field extension
scope_declines.reason: Normalization inside an arbitrary finite function-field extension is executed by the commutative-algebra normalization-finiteness-for-affine-domains page; AV-7 normalises only in the function field k(X) itself.

scope_declines.name: Application at the end of Lecture 9: a complete non-projective surface built from two blowups of P¹×P¹
scope_declines.reason: A completeness-versus-projectivity example unrelated to the divisor, strict-transform and curve-resolution claims of this pair; it is recorded here but not built.
